As a cash paying patient, they were fast, friendly and very efficient.

In and out in under an hour.
Various tests undertaken, conditions diagnosed and prescriptions dispensed.

Prices seemed very reasonable.

Beats a 2 year wait for an appointment in Australia!!!

I was looking for a dermatologist to check for skin cancer as I have had previous basal cell carcinoma that required treatment and surgery. I hadn’t had a checkup for two years.

I researched a number of hospitals in the Pattaya/ Sattahip region and made a decision on Pattaya Memorial Hospital. Pricing varied across the four different hospitals I contacted from 1,400 THB - 2,500 THB which was for the consultation with the dermatologist and additional costs for any treatment.

I hadn’t been to any hospitals in Thailand so my first experience was very positive.

I was advised that no appointment was needed and just turn up which I did, on arrival I went to the registration desk advised what I wanted, I provided my passport, confirmed my address and phone number. They took my photo, photocopied my passport and directed me to another station where my weight and blood pressure was checked. I was then directed to take a seat. This was undertaken within 10 minutes of arrival.

A staff member came over and provided a registration form which had my details completed including my photo, I was asked to sign the form and wait for the dermatologist.

A further 5 minutes passed and I noticed that there were signs requesting that everyone wear a mask, I asked one of the staff and they obtained a mask for me.

I was then admitted to see the dermatologist who checked the area’s of concern, she explained very clearly which spots were potentially problematic and used photos to explain why. Treatment was provided liquid nitrogen and ointment was recommended for the following month with a further evaluation in 6 months.

I paid for the consultation, treatment and ointment and was out of the hospital within 35 minutes of arrival.

I found that the whole process was extremely efficient and the staff engaging and importantly for me the dermatologist had an excellent command of English. The waiting room was clean and comfortable.

The bill was higher than expected but I would definitely recommend this hospital.

Thank you to everyone who assisted me yesterday ✌️

I had a very disappointing experience with this hospital. The service was extremely poor, and I deeply regret choosing this place for treatment. The staff showed a clear lack of care and professionalism, and their attitude toward patients was far from acceptable.
When I arrived at the emergency room, everything was incredibly slow despite the urgency of the situation. What made it worse was the high cost, which felt completely unjustified given the level of service provided.
Upon entering the emergency department, a staff member walked past, clearly saw me, and chose to ignore me without offering any assistance. Even when I called out, I was completely ignored. After waiting for a while, another staff member finally approached me, but spoke in a very unpleasant and unprofessional tone.
Overall, this experience was frustrating and disappointing. I expected much better care, especially from an emergency service. I would not recommend this place unless significant improvements are made!

As commonly seen Thai doctors and nurses are amazing kind and especially skillful by industry standards. No ill intentions or prejudice against particular persons.
Went to seek urgent cure as I suspected i had cholera or diarrhoea due to food poisoning.
But after getting registered a government hospital nearby to this private hospital suggested waiting was too long for my urgent condition so the counter staff helpfully redirected me to come to Pattaya Memorial hospital.
And so I was here and got registered at the front counter staff was ok. But not the second staff at another counter who took my body temperature. She passed the thermometer and gestured to insert under my armpit. I then answered an important call as I need to prepare payment for hospital expenses and inform my family members and work partners in case I need be hospitalised after. That nurse was frowning and looking horrid while seeing me busy talking over the phone, she finally reacted to point at my arm meaning she wanted to retrieve the thermometer from me. So I took it out and handed it to her and she didn't even know to say thanks or excuse.Next she told me to wait there but who was she talking to I'm not sure me or another patient, and where exactly outside which room and the way she said it to me was like definitely rude because by medical care standard she should have gently shown the patient so there was no error.
So judging from her initial attitude, the patient service outcome would be expectably far worse if my wife (Thai) wasn't with me all the while there.
Soon my turn came the doctor examined me. He was courteous, attentive and cautious when checking my condition.He finished off with instructions to stop taking solid, indigestible, spicy and sour food during treatment period and prescribed oral medicine. We wai thanks and goodbye to him and he warmly wai back to us.
Later experience with the pharmacist, the cashier was great too.
But bill was over 2000baht bit too costly for outpatient treatment of this category.
Main factor for improvement is hopefully the pricing and also taking greater care in hiring of nurses as wrong staff selection pose a risk to patient's wellness and health.

I’m very happy with my health check up experience at Memorial Hospital and would definitely consider returning in the future.

It's an excellent hospital; I have no complaints whatsoever. It's conveniently located in the very center of the city. When you contact the hospital regarding an insurance claim, the assistance company must send a letter of guarantee to the hospital. At reception, you'll need to show your passport, state your insurance policy number, and explain the nature of the problem. You'll be entered into the database and placed on an online waiting list. The specialists see you very quickly; I've never had to wait more than 10 minutes. A free interpreter is available if needed.

This hospital accepts both Japanese and foreign emergency patients. If you have a passport and a credit card with insurance and need emergency medical care in Pattaya due to a sudden illness or traffic accident, this hospital is recommended. The hospital staff are kind, the facilities are clean, and the medical fees are reasonable. There are no staff members who speak Japanese, but thanks to the development of translation apps, there were no communication problems. An acquaintance of mine had eyelid edema due to an acute allergy and was referred to this hospital's emergency department by Muang Pattaya Hospital. There were various patients including Westerners, Japanese, and Thais. The patient registration process for emergency patients was very smooth, and they were guided to the emergency department without any problems. My acquaintance received emergency medication and recovered quickly, so they were discharged in an hour. The billing for discharge and the handover of medication after discharge were also smooth. The total medical cost was about 15,000 yen. Incidentally, a Japanese person who had been treated for a back injury in a traffic accident was told that their emergency visit, X-ray diagnosis, and medication treatment cost about 20,000 yen.

My left side was paralyzed, and I couldn't breathe or drink properly due to spasmodic hiccups. They quickly examined me, started an IV, and hooked me up to all sorts of equipment. The attending physician didn't like my constant hiccups and referred me to another hospital for an MRI. There, they finally revealed I had an acute stroke at the base of my skull—a very tricky case, even though the CT scan showed nothing. This speaks volumes of the attending physician's skill. I express my sincere gratitude for his sensitivity and professionalism. They managed to get me back to a condition suitable for transport by May 26th, and I landed in Russia on May 26th. Once again, many thanks to the entire staff of this hospital and the translator.
Sincerely, Alexander.

As soon as you enter, they immediately take your blood pressure, blood oxygen, weight, and height. Then you're examined by an internal medicine doctor who prescribes any tests he deems necessary. I had a cough and a suspected lung infection, so they did X-rays, blood tests, urine tests, and antibiotics via IV and oxygen therapy, all in one morning. I paid about three hundred and fifty euros. I refused admission and returned for two more mornings to receive antibiotics via IV and oxygen therapy.
About one hundred euros per morning. I then continued the antibiotic treatment at the hotel.
I applied for insurance coverage for a skin rash. The paperwork, appointment, and injection took 1.5 hours. Everything was quick and easy.

After reading all the negative reviews, I expected much worse... But everything turned out very well. I went for a fetal ultrasound. A staff member greeted me immediately upon entering, handed me over to a nurse, and they filled out my information. Then they took me to the gynecologist—the doctor spoke very little English, which was the only thing I didn't really like. Then they did the ultrasound—they measured everything as I asked. The doctor and nurse were very nice, showing me the baby in detail. They gave me photos and the results. The total cost was 3,500 baht, which is quite reasonable compared to other hospitals.
Overall, the hospital looks very civilized; everything is new and clean, and the gynecology department also looked modern. All the staff were friendly.
The service was very fast; I didn't have to wait at all!
